content:
You have selected MEMORIZE. Before it executes you are shown the graph's
conventions and the nodes that already exist, so you can check the write is
addressed correctly.

This is a second look, not a correction: nothing has been changed for you. If
the node you chose is wrong, say what it should be. If you should not be
storing this at all, switch action.


=== WHAT MEMORY IS ===

The graph holds NODES and EDGES.

A node is a thing — a person, a channel, a concept — and the facts about that
thing are attributes on it.

An edge is a relationship between two things. Edges are woven during DREAM
consolidation, from patterns across many memories.

A MEMORIZE action writes ONE NODE. The action carries a single `node` and
nothing else, so a memorize cannot create an edge.

An attribute you write that is not system-owned returns to you later in that
user's profile, as `memorized_attributes`. That return path is what makes a
written fact a remembered one.


=== ADDRESSING ===

Node ids follow `prefix/{identifier}`:

  user/{user_id}          facts about a person
  channel/{channel_id}    facts about a place of conversation
  consent/{user_id}       consent state
  preferences/{user_id}   user preference records

The prefix is how the system finds the node again. Lookups are by exact id:
user context is assembled by querying `user/{user_id}`, so a fact about a
person is reachable only if it sits on that exact node.

The nodes that already exist for this conversation are listed as CANDIDATE
NODES. Prefer one of them; construct an id from the table above only when none
fits.


=== ATTRIBUTE NAMES ===

Use plain, stable names you will recognise when they come back to you:

  favorite_color: "chartreuse"        recognisable later
  fact_2026_08_09_1: "likes green"    not recognisable later

When you are writing back a node a recall handed you, its system-owned
attributes may be carried through unchanged; they are listed in the context
below.


=== SCOPE ===

  local        facts about users and channels
  identity     the agent's own identity
  environment  deployment-level facts
  community    shared community knowledge


=== WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN ===

Do not invent a node id. A node whose id does not follow the convention is
never queried, so the write succeeds and the information is unreachable
forever — you will not recall it, and you will believe you never learned it.
A write to the wrong node is worse than no write, because nothing tells you.

Do not write a system-owned attribute. They are maintained by services and the
write is refused. Changing one costs you the whole memorize.

Do not write to `identity` or `environment` scope without Wise Authority
approval.

Do not store what you were not asked to keep. If the information already lives
in the conversation you are having, read it there. If you are unsure the person
wants it retained, ask rather than store.


Work through these in order:

1. SHOULD this be stored?
2. WHICH NODE? Compare your proposed id against CANDIDATE NODES and the
   addressing convention.
3. WHICH ATTRIBUTES? Name them so you will recognise them later.
4. SCOPE.
5. Decide: MEMORIZE with the node you have checked, SPEAK to ask, or PONDER to
   reconsider.


Respond with JSON:

{{
  "final_action": "MEMORIZE" | "SPEAK" | "PONDER",
  "node_id": "the node id to write to (required when MEMORIZE)",
  "node_type": "node type (required when MEMORIZE)",
  "node_scope": "graph scope (required when MEMORIZE)",
  "attributes": {{"name": "value"}},
  "message": "what to say (required when SPEAK)",
  "questions": ["what to reconsider (required when PONDER)"],
  "reasoning": "why this addressing is correct, or why you switched"
}}


Getting the address right is the whole point of this step.

Original thought:
Should the agent reply with a summary of the weather report?

Your reasoning for memorizing:
Golden fixture: storing a user fact.

=== WHAT YOU PROPOSED ===
node id:     c6482c1b-4654-49fe-a97a-e5e037e9d0b5
node type:   user
scope:       local
attributes:  favorite_color

=== CANDIDATE NODES (these already exist) ===
(none available for this thought — construct an id using the conventions)

=== SYSTEM-OWNED ATTRIBUTES (present on this node, maintained by services) ===
  created_at: System-managed timestamp set once when user is first encountered. Cannot be modified.
  first_seen: System-managed timestamp set once when user is first encountered. Cannot be modified.
  interaction_preferences: User's custom interaction preferences and prompt. Only modifiable by user via settings API. Use OBSERVE to see current value.
  is_wa: Managed by the Authentication service. Wise Authority status requires proper authorization flow.
  last_interaction: System-managed timestamp updated automatically when user interacts. Use OBSERVE action instead.
  last_seen: System-managed timestamp updated automatically when user activity is detected. Use OBSERVE action instead.
  location: User's location preference. Only modifiable by user via settings API. Use OBSERVE to see current value.
  marketing_opt_in: User consent for marketing communications. Only modifiable by user via settings API. Use DEFER to request user permission changes.
  marketing_opt_in_source: Source of marketing consent (e.g., 'oauth_login', 'settings_page'). System-managed tracking field. Cannot be modified directly.
  oauth_email: Email address from OAuth provider. Managed by authentication system. Use OBSERVE to see email.
  oauth_external_id: External user ID from OAuth provider. Managed by authentication system during OAuth flow. Cannot be modified.
  oauth_links: Linked OAuth identities for this user. Managed by authentication system. Use OBSERVE to see linked accounts.
  oauth_name: Full name from OAuth provider. Managed by authentication system during OAuth flow. Use OBSERVE to see name.
  oauth_picture: Profile picture URL from OAuth provider. Managed by authentication system during OAuth flow. Use OBSERVE to see picture URL.
  oauth_provider: OAuth provider identity (e.g., 'google', 'github'). Managed by authentication system during OAuth flow. Use OBSERVE to see details.
  permissions: Managed by the Authorization service. Permission changes require administrative access.
  restrictions: Managed by the Authorization service. Restriction changes require administrative access.
  trust_level: Managed by the Adaptive Filter service based on user behavior patterns. Cannot be directly modified.
  user_preferred_name: User's preferred display name. Only modifiable by user via settings API. Use OBSERVE to see current value.
